geometry_edits.rationale: Enlarge the courtyard slightly to strengthen the public ground figure at the access edge.
Align the void opening with the west access side to reinforce the street-facing threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Slightly enlarge the court/void so the access-side public space reads more clearly as a usable neighborhood threshold rather than a narrow subtraction.
Keep the courtyard opening aligned with the verified access side so the public void addresses the street edge rather than turning inward.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing: one bent bar / folded wedge-like body sits clearly inside the parcel and responds to the access edge with a meaningful open seam rather than a sealed box. The top view confirms the dominant gesture and the void are consistent across views, and there is no obvious illegal collision of solids. However, the form is still somewhat abstract and sectionally unresolved for neighborhood living; it needs a clearer active ground/court articulation and a slightly more legible program threshold at the access edge. It is program-plausible because it can support mixed-use neighborhood living with a public court, but it does not yet strongly express a richer ground-hierarchy or an especially resolved upper/roof section. Reference resonance is moderate to strong: the candidate shares the courtyard/void and interlocking-mass logic of the similar references, while remaining less articulated than the best precedents.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and sculptural than the candidate; do not copy the roof articulation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise massing with a carved central void and a bridged upper connection creates a clear public threshold while keeping one dominant volume legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Aerial campus condition is broader than this compact candidate; avoid over-fragmenting into many parts.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A clustered court composition can scale to neighborhood program when the void organizes the whole figure and the edge masses remain readable.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is much flatter and more transparent; the candidate is more compressed and sectional.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated massing with a central void and continuous horizontal spread supports public circulation and mixed-use ground relation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more campus-like and distributed than the candidate; use it for section/terrace logic, not for splitting the mass too much.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced and connected wings can express neighborhood hierarchy while preserving a shared public core.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has more explicit multiple wings; the candidate should keep one dominant gesture rather than emulate the full complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a large carved void and setback upper masses create a legible public interior and strong hierarchy.
